chunks: And by this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saw a man intensely mourning his son, so he said:

O you! You have mourned over the minor calamity and been heedless of the major calamity. Had you prepared yourself for what happened to your son, your mourning would not have been so intense. Your calamity in abandoning preparedness for it is greater than your calamity over your son.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about mourning and preparing for death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) encountered a man overwhelmed with grief over his deceased son and offered a profound teaching on the nature of true loss. He reframed the man's situation by explaining that death itself is the lesser calamity; the greater calamity is failing to prepare for the inevitability of death. This teaching emphasizes the Islamic concept that one's spiritual unpreparedness for the afterlife is a far greater tragedy than the temporal loss of a loved one.

en.bilal-muhammad: And by this isnad. Al-Sadiq (as) saw a man intensely mourning his son, so he said: O you! You have mourned over the minor calamity, but you have been heedless of the major calamity. Had you prepared yourself for what would happen to your son, your mourning would not have been as intense. Your calamity of abandoning preparedness for this is greater than your calamity over your son.
